item.title: BRICS’ role in stability hailed amid intl shocks
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BRICS’ role in economic stability hailed amid intl shocks BRICS can serve as a potential stabilizer for the Global South as emerging economies grapple with overlapping shocks — from climate-driven disruptions to geopolitical conflict and a resurgence of protectionism — that are straining growth and investment, experts say. According to Priyanka Kishore, director and principal economist at the Singapore-based consultancy Asia Decoded, BRICS plays an important role in facilitating dialogue and information-sharing among major emerging economies. For Amitendu Palit, a senior research fellow with the Institute of South Asian Studies at the National University of Singapore, BRICS' biggest appeal is the organization's economic size. The group's 11 members and 10 partner countries account for more than 40 percent of global GDP, giving it the weight to expand trade and investment flows across regions. Greater intra-BRICS commerce would benefit not only the members themselves but also the wider economic zones they anchor, Palit said. Still, he noted that the bloc is far from cohesive enough to function as a rules-based free trade area: its members are geographically dispersed and operate under vastly different political systems, institutions and production standards. On the other hand, those divergences are also what make BRICS a "unique grouping", he said. "If it is able to move forward on its agenda of encouraging more trade in local currencies among members and enhancing food security, then it should be able to provide some solutions to unilateral trade actions elsewhere." Despite its limitations, BRICS, as an intergovernmental organization of developing countries, provides "concrete, nonalignment-friendly mechanisms" to cushion member economies against external vulnerabilities, according to Jaziri Alkaf Abdillah Suffian, chairman of BRICS International Malaysia and a former senator in Malaysia's parliament. Mechanisms developed under BRICS allow full members and partner states to settle bilateral trade using local currencies, he said, and local currency settlements can mitigate exchange rate risk and foreign currency liquidity squeezes during global market crashes. The most recent example of this saw President Xi Jinping and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi welcome the renewal of a bilateral local currency swap agreement and the expansion of the swap scale. The agreement was reached in Cairo when Xi made a state visit to Egypt earlier this month. BRICS has accelerated its push to widen its presence across the Global South. It admitted Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates in early 2024, its biggest expansion since its inception. Indonesia joined as the newest full member in January 2025. India is this year's rotating chair of BRICS, with New Delhi hosting the 18th BRICS Summit. This year's theme is "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability". The summit comes as the Global South faces threats from extreme weather as a result of a likely super El Nino, higher tariffs imposed by the United States, and an escalating crisis in the Middle East that has greatly raised global oil prices. Some economists have said rising demand for artificial intelligence has boosted exports of countries that rank higher in the technology value chain, dampening the impact of higher US tariffs on their economies. This is where BRICS can have a "more meaningful impact", Kishore of Asia Decoded said. Intra-BRICS trade has been rising for the past 20 years, but it still accounts for only about 5 percent of global trade, she said. "By reaffirming its commitment to free trade and strengthening trade engagement between members through instruments such as the proposed BRICS invoice discounting mechanism, it can help member countries diversify away from the US market," she said. prime@chinadailyapac.com

item.title: US firms display new confidence in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
US firms display new confidence in China Improved financial performance and easing China-US tensions have lifted confidence among United States businesses in China to its highest level after 2021, according to a survey report released on Thursday, signaling a brighter corporate outlook as bilateral trade relations stabilize. The share of respondents who are optimistic about their five-year business outlook in China rose by 17 percentage points to 58 percent, reversing a four-year decline that had pushed the reading to successive record lows, according to the 2026 China Business Report, released by the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai. In contrast, 16 percent of respondents are pessimistic about their five-year business outlook in China, the lowest level since 2021, said the report. It suggested that the improvement in business confidence has coincided with the easing of China-US trade tensions. However, US companies remain cautious about their business in China, keeping a close eye on the market environment and bilateral relations. This year's survey followed several months of positive developments in China-US relations. According to the report, these developments signal a move toward a more predictable and constructive bilateral relationship anchored in strategic stability. "Business confidence has made a critical comeback, supported by stronger financial performance and an improved geopolitical landscape," Jeffrey Lehman, chair of the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai, and Eric Zheng, president of AmCham Shanghai, said in a joint message. According to Lehman and Zheng, optimism about the five-year business outlook in China and the proportion of members reporting profitability last year both reached record levels. Furthermore, a growing percentage of respondents expect their top-line growth to improve this year and outpace their companies' global performance in the near term. Meanwhile, "investment sentiment has recovered, with nearly one-third of respondents planning to increase investment this year", the message added. Profitability among the surveyed companies reached its strongest level since 2019, as 78 percent of respondents were profitable in 2025, up 7 percentage points from the previous year, said the report. Due to differentiated industry dynamics and operating environments, performance continued to vary significantly by sector. Manufacturing, for example, remained the strongest-performing sector, with 85 percent of respondents reporting profits in 2025, a 5-percentage-point increase from the previous year. Services recorded the lowest rate among sectors at 69 percent, but showed a significant year-on-year improvement, rising 14 percentage points. Fifty-five percent of the respondents said that the business environment in China is transparent, up 7 percentage points, the report showed. "China will continue to open its economy wider to the world during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, while taking further steps to improve the business environment for foreign investors and ensure national treatment for foreign-invested enterprises," said Zhou Haibing, deputy head of the National Development and Reform Commission, during a roundtable meeting of the NDRC and US multinational enterprises in Beijing on Thursday. Stressing the mutually beneficial nature of China-US economic and trade ties, Zhou said that a stable and predictable relationship serves the interests of both countries and the wider world. China is home to 84,000 US-invested companies, with a combined annual revenue of nearly $700 billion, highlighting the strong complementarity and mutual benefits underpinning bilateral economic ties, he said. Given the sheer scale of bilateral economic and trade cooperation, differences and frictions are only natural, Zhou added, noting that solutions can always be found as long as the two sides respect and understand each other and strengthen communication and consultation. US companies' confidence in growth and investment in China comes as foreign companies continue to expand their investment in the country, Xinhua News Agency reported, citing Yan Dong, vice-minister of commerce. The number of new foreign-invested enterprises in China grew 4.4 percent year-on-year during the first seven months of this year, with foreign direct investment in actual use amounting to 438.33 billion yuan ($65.35 billion), according to the Ministry of Commerce. The increase was accompanied by an optimization in the investment structure, with investment in high-tech industries up 32.7 percent year-on-year, accounting for 41.6 percent of the total. "China is a training ground for US companies to maintain their global competitiveness," Lehman and Zheng from AmCham Shanghai said in their joint message. Chinese competitors raise the bar even higher. In the artificial intelligence sector, 43 percent of members view their local competitors as more advanced in AI adoption, the message added. wang_ying@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: BRICS ties deliver tangible benefits
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BRICS ties deliver tangible benefits Under the bright lights of an operating room at a hospital in Xiamen, Fujian province, Eric Rodrigo Morales Mercado, a Brazilian cardiologist, performs a minimally invasive cardiac procedure alongside Chinese doctors, gaining hands-on experience that he hopes to bring back to Brazil. The Brazilian doctor is in China as a visiting scholar under the Heart Sapling Program, a special initiative launched to strengthen medical cooperation among BRICS countries and help train young doctors from the Global South. For Mercado, the value of the experience is not measured in diplomatic communiques, but in what he can eventually take home. "Living and working in China changed absolutely the way that I see the world," he said. "For me, this is a life changer. We are here for a goal, and this goal is to learn some technique (and) bring that to our country." The program encapsulates a broader vision advanced by President Xi Jinping — that BRICS cooperation should translate into tangible benefits for people across the Global South. In 2017, when BRICS leaders gathered in Xiamen, Xi called for the partnership to "open the door to a second 'Golden Decade'", and make BRICS cooperation benefit the people of its then five member countries as well as the people of other countries. Speaking at a virtual BRICS summit in September 2025, Xi again called for member countries of the grouping to leverage their respective strengths, deepen practical cooperation and make business, financial, scientific and technological cooperation more productive, in order to strengthen the foundation, momentum and impact of greater BRICS cooperation and deliver more practical benefits. From Saturday to Sunday, Xi will attend the 18th BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi, India, during which he will put forward key Chinese proposals and initiatives to chart the course for the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. Mao Ning, spokeswoman for the Chinese Foreign Ministry, said that China stands ready to work with all BRICS parties to ensure that greater cooperation moves forward steadily and to contribute to building a community with a shared future for humanity. Over the past decade, BRICS has expanded both in terms of membership and areas of cooperation, moving beyond economic coordination into health, trade, technology, innovation and other sectors. BRICS countries now account for nearly half of the world's population, about 40 percent of global GDP and over one-fourth of global trade. He Yun, a senior researcher at the Belt and Road Institute of Tsinghua University, said the past decade has seen BRICS cooperation undergo important changes — from mechanism-building to more practical cooperation, from the original five members to a broader "BRICS Plus" framework, and from an economic coordination platform toward an important platform for Global South participation in global governance. "China's role in BRICS cooperation goes beyond its economic weight. It has simultaneously acted as an advocate of new ideas, a builder of cooperation mechanisms and a provider of public goods," she said. The senior researcher noted that China has promoted BRICS cooperation on poverty reduction, food security, the digital economy, industrialization and green development, including efforts to align these areas with the United Nations' 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. "China's contribution has been not only to put forward ideas and a vision for cooperation among Global South countries, but also to turn those ideas into institutions, platforms and projects," she said. Since 2017, China has launched a host of mechanisms to promote BRICS cooperation, including the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center, the China Center for Cooperation on Development of Special Economic Zones in BRICS Countries, and the China Center for BRICS Industrial Competencies. Zhou Ying, chief of the International Cooperation Division of the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center, said the fundamental change brought by BRICS expansion is not simply an increase in membership, but a significant broadening of the substance of cooperation and the needs of participating nations. A key mandate of the center is to help more Chinese enterprises expand their reach into BRICS countries. Under the platform's facilitation, Chinese companies have traveled to Brazil specifically to source coffee beans, helping more Brazilian coffee farmers gain access to the vast Chinese market, Zhou said. "We have also helped Chinese automakers enter the Ethiopian market, enabling more Chinese new energy vehicles to hit the streets of Ethiopia," Zhou added. Marcos Caldeira, a Brazilian businessman who first arrived in Xiamen in 2013, has seen his business increase with the expansion of BRICS cooperation. Caldeira, who comes from Vitoria, one of Brazil's major centers for the natural stone industry, said his business began by connecting Brazilian stone suppliers with the Chinese market. As the relationship developed, the flow began moving in both directions, linking producers and consumers in the two countries. After the BRICS summit in Xiamen in 2017, Caldeira's business received a boost. Today, two or three vessels carrying Brazilian stone arrive in China each month, he said, adding that smoother trade allows him to offer better prices to customers. "It's like a chain, so everything works much more smoothly." For Caldeira, BRICS is, therefore, not an abstract international grouping. Instead, it signifies ships leaving ports, workers processing stone, businesses finding customers and consumers gaining access to products. "I hope more countries can join BRICS, because more countries (means) more business, more opportunity, more trading," he said. With China set to assume BRICS' rotating presidency in 2027, a decade after the Xiamen summit, expectations are running high that Beijing will continue promoting BRICS cooperation toward a greater scope and more tangible outcomes. During a meeting in July, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said that China stands ready to work with BRICS partners to promote prosperity through development, stability through security, mutual trust through exchanges among civilizations and fairness through better global governance. Together, the BRICS countries will open up a future of peace and prosperity, Wang added. At the 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting in August, Li Chenggang, China's international trade representative and vice-minister of commerce, said that China is ready to deepen cooperation with BRICS members in trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, the digital economy, trade in services, green minerals, artificial intelligence and special economic zones. China will also explore institutional arrangements for economic and trade cooperation as well as economic integration, promote the high-quality development of expanded BRICS cooperation, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Li said. He Yun, the Tsinghua University researcher, said that China's rotating presidency of BRICS in 2027 will be particularly significant, as the "Greater BRICS" cooperation mechanism will enter a new stage, shifting from expanding its scale to improving governance and enhancing effectiveness. "In promoting BRICS cooperation, China has fully leveraged its strengths in markets, industry, technology and financing while respecting the development needs of other members and encouraging all countries to jointly propose projects, formulate rules and share the benefits," she said. "China's role in 2027 should be that of a coordinator of consensus, a builder of institutions and a provider of public goods." Olugbenga Abiodun, a cardiologist from Nigeria, which is a BRICS partner country, said he believes the BRICS health cooperation program launched by China will help improve the West African country's healthcare system and, eventually, its whole economy. Abiodun, who is also a participant of the Heart Sapling Program, said many Nigerian patients still travel abroad for advanced medical treatment, and training more specialists in Nigeria could help change that. "If a large number of Nigerian doctors are appropriately trained, and their specialist capacity is increased, then there won't be any reason for Nigerians to go outside the shores of the country to seek quality healthcare," he said. Abiodun also said that he sees room for broader cooperation with China in healthcare financing, low-cost medical technologies, equipment and consumables, generic pharmaceuticals and supply chains. "It's a life-changing program. It has improved my abilities, my capacity. This is a brilliant initiative by the BRICS community," he added. Contact the writers at xuwei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi to attend BRICS summit in New Delhi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
Xi to attend BRICS summit in New Delhi Meeting expected to boost cooperation, amplify voice of Global South, say experts President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi from Saturday to Sunday at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a Foreign Ministry spokesperson announced on Thursday. The meeting is widely expected to inject fresh momentum into BRICS cooperation, help BRICS countries and the wider Global South expand the pie of win-win cooperation, and reaffirm their commitment to multilateralism, experts said. India has adopted "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability" as the theme of its 2026 BRICS presidency, with a stated emphasis on a people-centric approach and stronger cooperation among countries of the Global South. Initially comprising Brazil, Russia, India and China, the grouping later welcomed South Africa and has since expanded further to 11 members. According to figures published on India's official BRICS presidency website, the 11 members account for about 49.5 percent of the world's population, 40 percent of global GDP and 26 percent of global trade. "Xi's attendance once again demonstrates the importance that China consistently attaches to BRICS cooperation, the development of the mechanism and the common development of Global South countries," said Su Xiaohui, an associate research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies. China's role in advancing BRICS cooperation will again be highlighted at the summit, she said. Cooperation with other BRICS countries has long been a priority of China's foreign policy. Xi's first appearance at a major international multilateral meeting after becoming Chinese president was at the fifth BRICS Summit, held in Durban, South Africa, in March 2013. Wang Youming, a researcher on developing countries at the China Institute of International Studies, said the upcoming summit holds particular significance, as it coincides with the 20th anniversary of the launch of BRICS cooperation. "One of the biggest highlights will be Xi's trip to India after seven years," Wang said. "China and India are not only close neighbors, but also founding members and major participants in BRICS. The state of their relationship has a direct bearing on the development of the mechanism." China and India have expressed mutual support for each other in hosting BRICS events, with India holding the rotating presidency this year and China set to assume the presidency next year. "Multilateral platforms can create opportunities for bilateral engagement, while improving bilateral relations can in turn facilitate coordination within multilateral mechanisms," Wang said. At a time when unilateral trade measures and disruptions to global industrial and supply chains are placing mounting pressure on developing economies, the summit is expected to amplify the voice of the Global South and strengthen coordination in upholding an open world economy and the multilateral trading system, he added. Wang said BRICS cooperation had gradually moved beyond broad policy declarations toward concrete programs involving small and medium-sized enterprises, cities, young people and people-to-people exchanges. According to Wang, emerging sectors such as the digital economy, green development and artificial intelligence are also likely to provide new areas of growth for BRICS cooperation. Emmanuel Frimpong Sarpong, who holds a PhD from the University of Nottingham Ningbo China and is the lead author of a study on China's role in BRICS, said China has played an instrumental role in the development of the BRICS mechanism. He described the New Development Bank as one of the grouping's most significant achievements. By the end of 2025, the bank had approved $42.9 billion in financing for 139 projects covering clean energy, transportation, water and sanitation, environmental protection, and social and digital infrastructure, according to the bank. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: China shakes, stirs Asia's best bars list
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
At Asia's 50 Best Bars awards ceremony in Macao this summer, the spotlight finally fell on an establishment tucked behind a traditional Cantonese storefront in Guangzhou's historic Dongshankou neighborhood. Hope & Sesame was named Asia's No 1 bar — the first time a venue on the Chinese mainland has taken top spot. "When they announced the No 3 bar, that feeling was already like being No 1 … So when they actually call you, it's very crazy," said Bastien Ciocca, one of the bar's co-founders. More significantly, it was not an isolated victory. The 2026 list featured seven bars from the Chinese mainland, with Hope & Sesame, MO Bar Shenzhen and Obsidian Bar, all in Guangdong province, ranked in the top 10. Other mainland entries that made the list were Pony Up in Shanghai, CMYK in Changsha, Hunan province, Ralph's Bar in Chengdu, Sichuan province, and Tiao in Beijing. The results represent the culmination of the local industry's development, with several mainland bars repeatedly recognized in recent years. Together, they point to broader growth. China's bar scene is expanding beyond Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangdong's Guangzhou and Shenzhen into regional cities, developing distinctive local expressions and boosting exchanges with the global industry. Beyond major cities Liu Ming, co-founder of CMYK, has worked in the bar industry for 27 years and divides the development of the cocktail scene into three stages. "The domestic cocktail industry has changed dramatically since I returned to China in 2012," he said. From 2012 to 2016, cocktail culture was concentrated mainly in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Chengdu, with foreign bartenders arriving to open venues and Chinese bartenders returning from overseas. Between 2016 and the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, cocktail bars spread to more cities, while Beijing and Shanghai developed increasingly international scenes. Liu said at that time there were at least 40 cocktail bars within walking distance of one another around Beijing's Sanlitun area, with more than 20 offering high-quality drinks. The post-pandemic period brought a third stage: rapid growth across the country, accompanied by a high closure rate of establishments. "The barriers to entry are too low," Liu said. "Many people lack experience in service, menu design and cost accounting, and they simply cannot make the numbers work." The geographical spread of the industry, however, is clearly changing. "When Asia's 50 Best Bars launched back in 2016, we noticed that all of the ranked bars were in what you'd consider 'cocktail capital cities'. Now, we're seeing real diversification," said Emma Sleight, head of content for Asia's 50 Best Bars. CMYK's continued presence on the list demonstrates that regional cities can build sustainable cocktail ecosystems, while destinations such as Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, are also beginning to attract international attention. The rankings also entice visitors to discover cities through their bar scenes. For regional venues, however, survival depends heavily on local tourism and foot traffic. Liu calculates that a 30-seat bar aiming to fill its seats every day needs roughly 210 to 300 customers a week. Relying entirely on regulars for survival is difficult. "For a large bar, you need regular customers to provide a safety net and tourists to add value," he said. He also believes bars need to form clusters. "The bar industry is an ecosystem. One bar dominating on its own simply doesn't work." Ralph's Bar in Chengdu represents another business model, bringing together the local expertise of Hope& Sesame and the resources and identity of luxury brand Ralph Lauren. "We see the fusion not as a simple mix of East and West, but as a dialogue between Ralph Lauren's American sensibility and the cultural energy of Chengdu," a Ralph Lauren spokesperson told China Daily. The spokesperson added: "The city's rich food and tea culture also sharpens our focus on texture, aroma and balance. Chengdu guests have exceptionally refined palates, so every ingredient must have a purpose."

item.title: UN chief warns against stoking Gulf tensions
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
UN chief warns against stoking Gulf tensions US, Iran trade strikes, while Trump says war could end after midterm elections United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has expressed concerns about the recent escalation in the Strait of Hormuz as the United States and Iran exchange their biggest waves of strikes on shipping in recent days. Stephane Dujarric, the UN chief's spokesman, highlighted the attacks against commercial vessels in the strait. "The secretary-general is deeply concerned by reports of further escalations in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the past days, including attacks against commercial vessels and threats of additional action against maritime and energy infrastructure," Dujarric said. He reiterated Guterres' appeal to all parties concerned to exercise utmost restraint and refrain from actions and rhetoric that could further inflame an already volatile situation. "Any further escalation risks grave consequences for civilians, regional stability, international peace and security, and the global economy," he said. Guterres is pushing for all parties to make full use of diplomatic channels and resolve issues through dialogue and negotiations, he added. "The United Nations Secretariat ... is ready to support all credible efforts aimed at de-escalation and a comprehensive and durable settlement." The concerns came as US President Donald Trump said the war could end immediately after the midterm elections in November, because Iran is unable to "hold out any longer". "Originally, I wanted to make a deal. We're so far down the line," he told reporters. "A negotiation could possibly happen, but it's not something we're looking at. This war will end immediately after our election," he added. The US and Iran were again locked in tit-for-tat strikes in the region, with Iranian oil tankers attacked and US bases facing strikes from Tehran. CBS News reported on Wednesday that several US aircraft were damaged in Iranian strikes on a US base in Jordan. Explosions were heard on Thursday in the coastal areas of southern Iran and on Qeshm Island, the Fars News Agency reported. Hassan Hassanzadeh, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in Greater Tehran, said Iran has "passed the stage of defensive and air defense confrontation". "Today we stand on the threshold of offensive operations, a turning point whose effects the enemies will soon understand," he said. Yahya Rahim Safavi, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader, said in a social media post that US warmongering had been "the best accelerator for the transfer of the weight of power and economic geography to the East". Pretending to have achieved victory is a sign of defeat and acceptance of the multipolarity of international power and security, he said. Despite escalating tensions, Iran's Foreign Ministry said Tehran is ready for dialogue with nations in the region to "foster mutual trust, achieve sustainable security and promote economic progress". Security in the Gulf and the Sea of Oman must be ensured through cooperation among littoral states and without the interference of foreign powers, the ministry said. Nuclear issue Meanwhile, for the first time in 20 years, the Board of Governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency approved on Wednesday a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for breaching its nonproliferation obligations. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi rejected the move. "They attack Iran's nuclear facilities under safeguards, disrupt the normal verification process, and then use that very disruption as a pretext to issue a resolution in the Board of Governors," Gharibabadi said on X. "With these fabrications, you can neither compensate for the failure of your policies and actions nor achieve anything in the Security Council," he said. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei slammed the decision as contradictory and baseless, saying it is "completely irrelevant" because Iran has remained compliant. Contact the writers at jan@chinadailyapac.com
